lesson_scope: Rearranging equations f(x)=0 into fixed-point iteration forms x=F(x), verifying algebraic equivalence in forward and reverse directions, assessing convergence conditions via |F'(x)| < 1, and understanding staircase and cobweb diagrams.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: rearranging a cubic equation into a square root fixed-point iteration form.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational practice of isolating x^2 to form a square root iteration.

hints: Start by isolating the highest power term $x^3$ on one side: $x^3 = 3x + 5$.
Since $x > 0$, divide both sides of $x^3 = 3x + 5$ by $x$ to express $x^2$ in terms of $x$.
Take the positive square root of both sides to conclude $x = \sqrt{3 + \dfrac{5}{x}}$.

walkthrough.text:
Take the square root of both sides, taking the positive root since $x > 0$:
$$x = \sqrt{3 + \dfrac{5}{x}}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Rearranges the cubic equation to make $x^2$ the subject, e.g. $x^3 = 3x + 5 \implies x^2 = 3 + \dfrac{5}{x}$ (or divides $x^3 - 3x - 5 = 0$ by $x$).
Takes the positive square root to obtain the given form $x = \sqrt{3 + \dfrac{5}{x}}$ with clear algebraic steps shown.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: rearranging an exponential-polynomial equation using natural logarithms.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Standard logarithm rearrangement to linearize the exponent and form an iteration.

hints: Take the natural logarithm ($\ln$) of both sides of the equation $x^3 = \mathrm{e}^{2x - 1}$.
Apply the power law $\ln(x^3) = 3\ln x$ and the inverse property $\ln(\mathrm{e}^{2x - 1}) = 2x - 1$.
Isolate $x$ from $3\ln x = 2x - 1$ and add iteration subscripts $n+1$ and $n$.

walkthrough.text:
Take the natural logarithm of both sides:
$$\ln(x^3) = \ln\left(\mathrm{e}^{2x - 1}\right)$$

Apply the logarithm laws $\ln(x^3) = 3\ln x$ and $\ln(\mathrm{e}^{2x - 1}) = 2x - 1$:
$$3\ln x = 2x - 1$$

Rearrange to make $x$ the subject and add subscripts:
$$2x = 3\ln x + 1 \implies x = \dfrac{1}{2}(3\ln x + 1)$$
Hence, $x_{n+1} = \dfrac{1}{2}(3\ln x_n + 1)$.

ai_rubric.observable: Takes the natural logarithm of both sides and applies laws of logarithms to obtain $3\ln x = 2x - 1$.
Makes $x$ the subject to obtain $x = \dfrac{1}{2}(3\ln x + 1)$ and correctly introduces iteration subscripts $x_{n+1} = \dfrac{1}{2}(3\ln x_n + 1)$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: rearranging a trigonometric equation using inverse trigonometric functions.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Rearranging x tan x = c into an arctan fixed-point iteration.

hints: Isolate the trigonometric term $\tan x$ by dividing both sides of $x\tan x = 3$ by $x$.
Apply the inverse tangent function $\tan^{-1}$ to both sides and attach the iterative subscripts $x_{n+1}$ and $x_n$.

walkthrough.text:
Divide both sides of $x\tan x = 3$ by $x$ (valid since $x \in (0, \pi/2)$ so $x \neq 0$):
$$\tan x = \dfrac{3}{x}$$

Apply the inverse tangent function $\tan^{-1}$ to both sides:
$$x = \tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{3}{x}\right)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Rearranges the equation to isolate $\tan x$, giving $\tan x = \dfrac{3}{x}$.
Applies the inverse tangent function to express $x = \tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{3}{x}\right)$ and writes the iterative formula $x_{n+1} = \tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{3}{x_n}\right)$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: proving that the limit of an iterative sequence satisfies the original algebraic equation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Reverse verification showing limit alpha satisfies the underlying polynomial.

hints: At convergence, the limit $\alpha$ satisfies $\lim_{n\to\infty} x_{n+1} = \lim_{n\to\infty} x_n = \alpha$. Substitute $\alpha$ for both $x_{n+1}$ and $x_n$.
Multiply both sides by $(3\alpha^2 - 1)$ to clear the denominator.
Expand the left side to get $3\alpha^3 - \alpha$ and rearrange all terms to one side to show $\alpha^3 - \alpha - 7 = 0$.

walkthrough.text:
Expand and rearrange:
$$3\alpha^3 - \alpha = 2\alpha^3 + 7 \implies 3\alpha^3 - 2\alpha^3 - \alpha - 7 = 0 \implies \alpha^3 - \alpha - 7 = 0$$
Thus, $\alpha$ satisfies the equation $x^3 - x - 7 = 0$.

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes $x_{n+1} = x_n = \alpha$ into the iterative formula to obtain $\alpha = \dfrac{2\alpha^3 + 7}{3\alpha^2 - 1}$ and clears the fraction.
Expands $\alpha(3\alpha^2 - 1) = 3\alpha^3 - \alpha$ and simplifies to $\alpha^3 - \alpha - 7 = 0$, concluding that $\alpha$ satisfies $x^3 - x - 7 = 0$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: applying the derivative convergence criterion |F'(x)| < 1 to justify convergence.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Assessing fixed-point iteration convergence by computing |F'(x)| at an approximate root.

hints: Differentiate $F(x) = (5 - 2x)^{1/3}$ with respect to $x$ using the chain rule: $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}[u^{1/3}] = \dfrac{1}{3}u^{-2/3} \cdot u'$.
Substitute $x = 1.33$ into $F'(x) = -\dfrac{2}{3(5 - 2x)^{2/3}}$ to calculate its numerical value.
State the convergence condition $|F'(\alpha)| < 1$ and observe that $|-0.38| < 1$, confirming convergence.

walkthrough.text: Since $|F'(1.33)| \approx 0.38 < 1$, the fixed-point iteration satisfies the convergence criterion $|F'(x)| < 1$ near the root, so the sequence converges to $\alpha$.

ai_rubric.observable: Correctly differentiates $F(x) = (5 - 2x)^{1/3}$ using the chain rule to obtain $F'(x) = -\dfrac{2}{3}(5 - 2x)^{-2/3}$.
Evaluates $F'(1.33) \approx -0.38$ (or $|F'(1.33)| \approx 0.38$) and concludes that the iteration converges because $|F'(1.33)| < 1$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: interpreting cobweb vs staircase geometric iteration behaviour and gradient magnitude.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Interpreting graphical iteration steps on y = x and y = F(x).

hints: Recall that when $F'(x) < 0$, successive iterations alternate above and below the root, forming an enclosed rectangular spiral known as a cobweb diagram.
Convergence occurs whenever the magnitude of the derivative satisfies $|F'(\alpha)| < 1$, causing each step towards the line $y = x$ to move closer to the root.

walkthrough.text: Identify the pattern: Because the gradient of $y = F(x)$ is negative ($F'(\alpha) = -0.4 < 0$), iterates oscillate between values greater than and less than the root, producing a cobweb (or spiral) pattern.
Explain convergence: The sequence converges because $|F'(\alpha)| = |-0.4| = 0.4 < 1$. Each reflection between $y = F(x)$ and $y = x$ contracts towards the point of intersection $(2, 2)$.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the diagram represents a cobweb (or spiral) pattern (due to the negative gradient $F'(x) < 0$).
Explains that the iteration converges because $|F'(\alpha)| = |-0.4| = 0.4 < 1$ (or because successive iterations spiral inwards towards the root $(2, 2)$).

Show vertical and horizontal line segments starting from x_0 = 1.6 on the x-axis, going vertically to y = F(x_0), horizontally to y = x, vertically to y = F(x_1), horizontally to y = x, illustrating a cobweb spiraling inwards toward (2, 2).

questions.difficulty_reason: Easy: multi-part question exploring two distinct algebraic rearrangements of a cubic polynomial.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Rearranging a cubic to a rational square-root fixed point formula.

hints: Isolate the highest power term $2x^3$ on the left-hand side: $2x^3 = 7x - 3$.
Divide both sides by $2x$ to express $x^2$ in terms of $x$.
Take the positive square root of both sides to obtain $x = \sqrt{\dfrac{7x - 3}{2x}}$.

walkthrough.text:
Isolate $2x^3$ on one side of the equation:
$$2x^3 = 7x - 3$$

Take the square root of both sides:
$$x = \sqrt{\dfrac{7x - 3}{2x}}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Isolates $2x^3 = 7x - 3$ and divides both sides by $2x$ to obtain $x^2 = \dfrac{7x - 3}{2x}$.
Takes the positive square root to complete the rearrangement to $x = \sqrt{\dfrac{7x - 3}{2x}}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Forming the simple polynomial iteration by isolating the linear term.

hints: Isolate the linear term $7x$ on one side of $2x^3 - 7x + 3 = 0$.
Divide by $7$ to make $x$ the subject and attach subscripts $x_{n+1}$ and $x_n$.

walkthrough.text:
Divide by $7$ and write in iterative notation:
$$x = \dfrac{2x^3 + 3}{7} \implies x_{n+1} = \dfrac{2x_n^3 + 3}{7}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Isolates $7x = 2x^3 + 3$, divides by $7$ to make $x$ the subject, and attaches recurrence subscripts to obtain $x_{n+1} = \dfrac{2x_n^3 + 3}{7}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: combines exponential-logarithmic algebraic rearrangement with chain rule differentiation and fixed-point convergence analysis.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Rearranging exponential equation by taking logs on both sides.

hints: Rearrange $\mathrm{e}^{2x} - 4x - 5 = 0$ so that the exponential term $\mathrm{e}^{2x}$ is isolated on one side.
Take the natural logarithm ($\ln$) of both sides to remove the exponential base $\mathrm{e}$.
Use $\ln(\mathrm{e}^{2x}) = 2x$ and divide by $2$ to express $x$ in terms of $\ln(4x + 5)$.

walkthrough.text:
Take natural logarithms of both sides:
$$\ln\left(\mathrm{e}^{2x}\right) = \ln(4x + 5)$$

Simplify using $\ln(\mathrm{e}^u) = u$ and solve for $x$:
$$2x = \ln(4x + 5) \implies x = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(4x + 5)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Isolates the exponential term $\mathrm{e}^{2x} = 4x + 5$ and takes the natural logarithm of both sides.
Applies $\ln(\mathrm{e}^{2x}) = 2x$ and divides by $2$ to complete the derivation of $x = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(4x + 5)$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Assessing convergence via chain rule derivative of logarithmic iteration function.

hints: Differentiate $F(x) = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(4x + 5)$ with respect to $x$ using the chain rule: $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}[\ln(u)] = \dfrac{u'}{u}$.
Substitute $x = 1.2$ into your expression for $F'(x)$ to find its numerical value.
Compare the magnitude $|F'(1.2)|$ to $1$: because $|F'(1.2)| < 1$, the fixed-point iteration condition for convergence is satisfied.

walkthrough.text: Since $|F'(1.2)| \approx 0.204 < 1$, the iteration satisfies $|F'(\alpha)| < 1$ near the root, guaranteeing convergence.

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates $F(x) = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(4x + 5)$ correctly using the chain rule to obtain $F'(x) = \dfrac{2}{4x + 5}$ (or $\dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{4}{4x + 5}$).
Evaluates $F'(1.2) \approx 0.204$ (or $10/49$) and concludes convergence since $|F'(1.2)| < 1$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: rigorous comparative convergence problem requiring trigonometric differentiation, inverse trig calculus, and identifying divergence.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Rearranging trigonometric equation into reciprocal iteration.

hints: Isolate $x$ by dividing both sides of $x\sin x = 1$ by $\sin x$.
Recall the reciprocal trigonometric definition $\operatorname{cosec} x = \dfrac{1}{\sin x}$.
Write the result in iterative form by attaching recurrence indices $x_{n+1}$ and $x_n$.

walkthrough.text:
Divide both sides of $x\sin x = 1$ by $\sin x$ (valid since $\sin x \neq 0$ for $x \in (\pi/6, \pi/2)$):
$$x = \dfrac{1}{\sin x}$$

Apply the reciprocal trigonometric identity $\dfrac{1}{\sin x} = \operatorname{cosec} x$:
$$x = \operatorname{cosec} x$$

ai_rubric.observable: Divides $x\sin x = 1$ by $\sin x$ to express $x = \dfrac{1}{\sin x}$ (valid for $x \in (\pi/6, \pi/2)$).
Uses the reciprocal identity $\dfrac{1}{\sin x} = \operatorname{cosec} x$ to write $x_{n+1} = \operatorname{cosec} x_n$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving that an alternative rearrangement diverges by demonstrating |F'(x)| > 1.

hints: Use the standard derivative formula $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}u}[\sin^{-1} u] = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^2}}$ with $u = \dfrac{1}{x}$.
Apply the chain rule with $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}[x^{-1}] = -\dfrac{1}{x^2}$.
Simplify the algebraic fraction by writing $\sqrt{1 - 1/x^2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{x^2 - 1}}{x}$ so that one factor of $x$ cancels.
Evaluate $F'(1.114)$ numerically and compare its absolute value with $1$.

walkthrough.text:
Simplify the square root term for $x > 1$:
$$\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{1}{x^2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{x^2 - 1}{x^2}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{x^2 - 1}}{x}$$
$$F'(x) = \dfrac{1}{\frac{\sqrt{x^2 - 1}}{x}} \cdot \left(-\dfrac{1}{x^2}\right) = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{x^2 - 1}} \cdot \left(-\dfrac{1}{x^2}\right) = -\dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{x^2 - 1}}$$
Since $|F'(1.114)| \approx 1.83 > 1$, the derivative magnitude exceeds $1$ at the root, which causes successive iterations to diverge away from $\alpha$.

ai_rubric.observable: Applies standard derivative of inverse sine with chain rule: $F'(x) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - (1/x)^2}} \cdot \left(-\dfrac{1}{x^2}\right)$.
Simplifies denominator $\sqrt{1 - 1/x^2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{x^2 - 1}}{x}$ and multiplies by $-\dfrac{1}{x^2}$ to obtain $F'(x) = -\dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{x^2 - 1}}$.
Evaluates $|F'(1.114)| \approx 1.83$ (or $F'(1.114) \approx -1.83$) and explains that the iteration diverges because $|F'(\alpha)| > 1$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: links geometric staircase diagram analysis with algebraic differentiation, quadratic roots, and derivative convergence conditions.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Rearranging a quadratic to a square-root fixed point iteration and finding the exact root.

hints: Isolate $2x^2$ in the equation $2x^2 - x - 6 = 0$ to get $2x^2 = x + 6$.
Divide by $2$ and take the positive square root to obtain $x = \sqrt{\dfrac{x + 6}{2}}$.
Factorise the quadratic $2x^2 - x - 6 = (2x + 3)(x - 2) = 0$ to find the positive root $\alpha$.

walkthrough.text:
Rearrange the quadratic equation to isolate $x^2$:
$$2x^2 = x + 6 \implies x^2 = \dfrac{x + 6}{2}$$

Solve $2x^2 - x - 6 = 0$ by factorisation:
$$(2x + 3)(x - 2) = 0 \implies x = -\dfrac{3}{2} \quad \text{or} \quad x = 2$$
Since $\alpha > 0$, the exact root is $\alpha = 2$.

ai_rubric.observable: Rearranges $2x^2 - x - 6 = 0$ to $2x^2 = x + 6$ and divides by $2$ to obtain $x = \sqrt{\dfrac{x + 6}{2}}$.
Factorises $(2x + 3)(x - 2) = 0$ (or applies quadratic formula) to identify the positive root $\alpha = 2$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Interpreting staircase behaviour from positive derivative and confirming convergence.

hints: Differentiate $F(x) = \left(\dfrac{x + 6}{2}\right)^{1/2}$ with respect to $x$ using the chain rule.
Substitute $\alpha = 2$ into $F'(x)$ to find the exact numerical gradient $F'(2)$.
Recall that when the gradient is positive ($F'(x) > 0$), the iteration values increase (or decrease) monotonically without oscillating, producing a staircase pattern.
Check that $|F'(2)| < 1$ to confirm that the steps get progressively closer to $(2, 2)$.

walkthrough.text:
Explain pattern and convergence:
Since $F'(2) = 0.125 > 0$, successive values of $x_n$ approach the root monotonically from one side, creating a staircase pattern.
Because $|F'(2)| = 0.125 < 1$, the distance to the root contracts at each iteration, confirming convergence to $2$.

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates $F(x) = \left(\dfrac{x + 6}{2}\right)^{1/2}$ using chain rule to get $F'(x) = \dfrac{1}{4}\left(\dfrac{x + 6}{2}\right)^{-1/2}$ (or $\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2x + 12}}$).
Evaluates $F'(2) = \dfrac{1}{8} = 0.125$.
Explains that $F'(2) > 0$ yields a monotonic staircase pattern, and $0 < F'(2) < 1$ (or $|F'(2)| < 1$) confirms convergence.

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: comparative analysis of two cubic rearrangements demonstrating rapid divergence when derivative magnitude greatly exceeds 1.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Isolating linear term to form convergent polynomial iteration.

hints: Isolate the linear term $3x$ on one side of $x^3 + 3x - 1 = 0$.
Divide by $3$ to make $x$ the subject.
Add iteration subscripts $x_{n+1}$ and $x_n$ to complete the iterative formula.

walkthrough.text:
Divide by $3$ and attach subscripts:
$$x = \dfrac{1 - x^3}{3} \implies x_{n+1} = \dfrac{1 - x_n^3}{3}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Isolates $3x = 1 - x^3$, divides by $3$ to make $x$ the subject, and attaches iteration subscripts $x_{n+1} = \dfrac{1 - x_n^3}{3}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving that cube-root rearrangement fails due to steep derivative near root.

hints: Differentiate $G(x) = (1 - 3x)^{1/3}$ with respect to $x$ using the chain rule.
Substitute $x = 0.32$ into $G'(x) = -\dfrac{1}{(1 - 3x)^{2/3}}$ to find its value.
Observe that $|G'(0.32)| \approx 8.55 \gg 1$, violating the convergence requirement $|G'(\alpha)| < 1$.

walkthrough.text: Since $|G'(0.32)| \approx 8.55 > 1$, errors multiply by a factor of over $8$ at each step, causing severe divergence away from $\alpha$.

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates $G(x) = (1 - 3x)^{1/3}$ using the chain rule to obtain $G'(x) = \dfrac{1}{3}(1 - 3x)^{-2/3}(-3) = -\dfrac{1}{(1 - 3x)^{2/3}}$.
Evaluates $|G'(0.32)| = \dfrac{1}{(0.04)^{2/3}} \approx 8.55$ and concludes that the iteration fails to converge because $|G'(\alpha)| > 1$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: full comparative analysis of dual transcendental rearrangements requiring simultaneous exponential and logarithmic differentiation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Deriving two distinct transcendental iteration schemes from x^2 e^x = k.

hints: To obtain the logarithmic formula, divide $x^2 \mathrm{e}^x = 8$ by $x^2$ to isolate $\mathrm{e}^x = \dfrac{8}{x^2}$, then take natural logarithms.
To obtain the square root formula, divide $x^2 \mathrm{e}^x = 8$ by $\mathrm{e}^x$ to get $x^2 = 8\mathrm{e}^{-x}$, then take the positive square root.
Attach recurrence subscripts $x_{n+1}$ and $x_n$ to both resulting equations.
Check that both formulas are algebraically equivalent to the original equation $x^2 \mathrm{e}^x = 8$.

ai_rubric.observable: Rearranges $x^2 \mathrm{e}^x = 8$ to $\mathrm{e}^x = \dfrac{8}{x^2}$ and takes natural logarithms to obtain $x_{n+1} = \ln\!\left(\dfrac{8}{x_n^2}\right)$.
Rearranges $x^2 \mathrm{e}^x = 8$ to $x^2 = 8\mathrm{e}^{-x}$ and takes the positive square root to obtain $x_{n+1} = \sqrt{8\mathrm{e}^{-x_n}}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving that the reciprocal nature of the two arrangements causes one derivative to be > 1 and the other < 1.

hints: Write $F(x) = \ln 8 - 2\ln x$ and differentiate: $F'(x) = -\dfrac{2}{x}$.
Write $G(x) = \sqrt{8}\,\mathrm{e}^{-x/2}$ and differentiate using chain rule: $G'(x) = -\dfrac{\sqrt{8}}{2}\,\mathrm{e}^{-x/2}$.
Substitute $\alpha \approx 1.34$ into both derivatives to find numerical values $F'(1.34)$ and $G'(1.34)$.
Apply the fixed-point convergence criterion $|F'(x)| < 1$ to conclude which sequence converges.

walkthrough.text:
Compare magnitudes:
$|F'(1.34)| \approx 1.49 > 1$, so the logarithmic iteration diverges.
$|G'(1.34)| \approx 0.67 < 1$, so the square root iteration $x_{n+1} = \sqrt{8\mathrm{e}^{-x_n}}$ converges to $\alpha$.

ai_rubric.observable: Finds derivatives $F'(x) = -\dfrac{2}{x}$ and $G'(x) = -\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\sqrt{8}\,\mathrm{e}^{-x/2} = -\dfrac{1}{2}G(x)$, evaluating $F'(1.34) \approx -1.49$ and $G'(1.34) \approx -0.67$.
Concludes that $x_{n+1} = \sqrt{8\mathrm{e}^{-x_n}}$ converges because $|G'(1.34)| < 1$, while $x_{n+1} = \ln\!\left(\dfrac{8}{x_n^2}\right)$ diverges because $|F'(1.34)| > 1$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: multi-root selective convergence theorem testing why a single rearrangement cannot find all roots and proving why a complementary rearrangement converges.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Testing derivative magnitude across multiple roots of a cubic.

hints: Differentiate $F(x) = \dfrac{x^3 + 1}{5}$ directly with respect to $x$ to get $F'(x) = \dfrac{3x^2}{5}$.
Substitute each of the three root estimates $\alpha_1 = -2.33$, $\alpha_2 = 0.20$, and $\alpha_3 = 2.13$ into $F'(x)$.
Check which of the three values satisfies the convergence condition $|F'(\alpha)| < 1$.
Conclude that only $\alpha_2$ produces a derivative with absolute value strictly less than $1$.

walkthrough.text:
Conclusion:
The iteration $x_{n+1} = \dfrac{x_n^3 + 1}{5}$ can only converge to the middle root $\alpha_2 \approx 0.20$.

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates $F(x) = \dfrac{x^3 + 1}{5}$ to obtain $F'(x) = \dfrac{3x^2}{5}$.
Calculates $F'(-2.33) \approx 3.26$, $F'(0.20) = 0.024$, $F'(2.13) \approx 2.72$ and concludes convergence only to $\alpha_2 \approx 0.20$ as $|F'(0.20)| < 1$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving that the inverted/cube-root rearrangement converges at the outer root.

hints: Differentiate $H(x) = (5x - 1)^{1/3}$ using the chain rule: $H'(x) = \dfrac{1}{3}(5x - 1)^{-2/3} \cdot 5$.
Notice that since $\alpha_3^3 - 5\alpha_3 + 1 = 0$, we have $5\alpha_3 - 1 = \alpha_3^3$, so $(5\alpha_3 - 1)^{2/3} = (\alpha_3^3)^{2/3} = \alpha_3^2$.
Substitute $\alpha_3 = 2.13$ into $H'(x) = \dfrac{5}{3x^2}$ to calculate $H'(2.13)$.
Verify that $|H'(2.13)| < 1$, proving that this cube-root iteration successfully converges to $\alpha_3$.

walkthrough.text:
Prove convergence:
Because $|H'(2.13)| \approx 0.368 < 1$, the iteration $x_{n+1} = (5x_n - 1)^{1/3}$ contracts errors by approximately $63\%$ per step, guaranteeing rapid convergence to the root $\alpha_3$.

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates $H(x) = (5x - 1)^{1/3}$ using chain rule to obtain $H'(x) = \dfrac{5}{3}(5x - 1)^{-2/3} = \dfrac{5}{3(5x - 1)^{2/3}}$.
Evaluates $H'(2.13) \approx 0.37$ (or $\dfrac{5}{3(2.13)^2}$) and concludes convergence to $\alpha_3$ since $|H'(2.13)| < 1$.
